name: יֶתֶר
summary: Borne by Jether, Gideon's firstborn, who as a youth was afraid to draw his sword on Zebah and Zalmunna (Jdg 8:20); by Jether the father of Amasa, called Jether the Ishmaelite in 1Ch 2:17 and, in the spelling יִתְרָא, Ithra the Israelite in 2Sa 17:25 (1Ki 2:5, 32); by a man of Judah who died without sons (1Ch 2:32); a son of Ezrah (1Ch 4:17); an Asherite, the Ithran of 1Ch 7:37 (1Ch 7:38); and once by Moses' father-in-law, elsewhere יִתְרוֹ (Exo 4:18). The name is the noun יֶתֶר, which Jacob uses of the firstborn: “my firstborn … יֶתֶר of dignity and יֶתֶר of power” (Gen 49:3). Scripture does not explain the name.

evidence.note: “He said to יֶתֶר his firstborn, Rise, kill them.”
“Reuben, you are my firstborn … יֶתֶר שְׂאֵת וְיֶתֶר עָז”: the noun the name is, said of a firstborn.
“Amasa was the son of a man named יִתְרָא the Israelite.”
“The father of Amasa was יֶתֶר the Ishmaelite.”
“Amasa the son of יֶתֶר”, whom Joab killed. So 1Ki 2:32.
“The sons of Jada: יֶתֶר and Jonathan; and יֶתֶר died without sons.”
“The sons of Ezrah: יֶתֶר and Mered …”
“The sons of יֶתֶר: Jephunneh, Pispah and Ara”, the Ithran of 7:37.
Moses “returned to יֶתֶר his father-in-law … and יִתְרוֹ said to Moses, Go in peace.”

note: Takes j.ef.ae (the name יֶתֶר, whose 35 tokens in the brief are all spellings יֶתֶר, most of them the noun “rest of”) and j.ef.af (יִתְרָא, 2Sa 17:25 only). TIPNR records the father of Amasa once (Jether@2Sa.17.25) under both spellings; the Asherite as Ithran@1Ch.7.37, who is also in names/ithran.json; Moses' father-in-law as Jethro@Exo.2.18, also in names/jethro.json and names/reuel.json. 2Sa 17:25 “the Israelite” against 1Ch 2:17 “the Ishmaelite” is left as the text has it. The reading “pre-eminence” or “abundance” takes the name as the noun; no verse gives its meaning.
